sentences.text: US death row inmate Christa Pike has released her first public statement since her botched execution in September.
sentences.article_title: US inmate Christa Pike says she woke up 'confused and in pain' after failed execution

sentences.text: "There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain," she said in the statement.

sentences.text: I still struggle to speak.

sentences.text: And the pain isn't just physical.

sentences.text: There is pain in my mind and in my soul." Pike, 50, was discharged from hospital at the end of last month after surviving two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital, which left her in a critical condition.

sentences.text: Christa Pike survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbita She has since been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years for murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995.

sentences.text: "But healing is not the same as being okay." Her lawyers previously said she had suffered from pneumonia following the attempted execution, had significant swelling on her arms and was also unable to swallow.

sentences.text: Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for low-income young people.

sentences.text: "I had not contemplated life beyond that night, and I'm deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position," she said in her statement.

sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Over the nine-week period, "root-to-tip" dishes made up a third of total daily hot menu sales at the university.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Those choosing the new dishes were less likely to finish their meals than diners eating from the conventional menu.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Green potatoes and rhubarb leaves contain toxic compounds, while tough stalks and seeds may not be suitable for young children.

sentences.text: Nicola Shaw had been criticised over Yorkshire Water's pay and performance Yorkshire Water's chief executive has announced she is to step down, just 24 hours after the company was given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Nicola Shaw, who has led the firm since 2022, will leave the role on 1 January to be replaced by Nicola Medalova, a chartered environmental health officer who previously worked for the National Grid.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: In a statement on Friday, Shaw said it had been a "privilege" to lead the company but that it was the "right time" to leave her post.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: The payments were made by Yorkshire Water's parent company, Kelda Holdings, for what the firm said was "investor engagement" and "financial oversight".
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: The EA said Yorkshire Water was responsible for 260 pollution incidents in 2025, which was its highest total since 2011.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: In 2024, Ofwat announced it was fining the company £47m for historic sewage leaks .
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: In her statement, Shaw said: "It has been a privilege to lead Yorkshire Water and serve the people of Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: She said: "I am delighted to be joining Yorkshire Water and grateful to the board for the opportunity to lead the business through its next chapter.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: She received a further £660,000 earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Ofwat said the payments were not performance-related.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: The previously undisclosed payments had come to light the previous August when the government banned Yorkshire Water and five other water companies from paying "unfair" bonuses to bosses .
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Tom Gordon, Liberal Democrat MP for Harrogate and Knaresborough, said Shaw should have stepped down "much earlier".
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Nicola Shaw oversaw abysmal management of our precious natural resources, trashing our rivers while receiving an eye-watering salary," he said.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "A new face at the top cannot wash away years of Yorkshire Water failing to put customers first," she said.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "Nicola Shaw's time as Yorkshire Water boss saw customers frustrated by poor service, skyrocketing bills, record pollution incidents, and a plummet from 'good' to the worst possible one-star environment rating.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "There must be a wholesale shift in culture that finally prioritises customers.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Only then can the company begin to restore public trust." Robbie Moore, Conservative MP for Keighley and Ilkley, said Shaw's resignation "could not have come quick enough".
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: He added: "I have therefore already requested an urgent meeting with the new CEO Designate Nicola Medalova to understand how she plans to improve Yorkshire Water's performance at speed.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "The status quo cannot continue." Chris Stewart at York campaign group Ouse It Lose It said the new CEO's priority had to be looking at "failures in the system".
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "There's been a continual decline in the operation of this business," he said.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "Clearly things are going wrong." Stewart said he was not surprised by Shaw's resignation but it was a "shocking indictment of the way the company has been performing, while making loud noises about how much they're putting into improving".
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Naomi Tilley, campaigns manager at protest group Surfers Against Sewage, said "systematic change" was needed to fix the company.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "Regardless of who the CEO is, there's sewage entering the sea and the water companies are failing.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Yorkshire Water is not an outlier," said Tilley.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: "The whole system and every water company is failing in different ways and we are seeing that the system is broken and we need fundamental change.
sentences.article_title: Yorkshire Water boss resigns after firm downgraded

sentences.text: Achill Island Coast Guard volunteers abseiled down a steep cliff to reach the couple A couple who went for a beach walk shortly after getting engaged had to be rescued by the Irish Coast Guard after an incoming tide trapped them against a coastal cliff.

sentences.text: The bride and groom-to-be were hauled approximately 150m (490 ft) to the top of the cliff to safety because rescuers could not reach them by boat or by helicopter.

sentences.text: The dramatic rescue took place during gale-force winds on Achill Island, off the west coast of Ireland, on Monday afternoon.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: Coast Guard volunteer Peter McManamon, who coordinated the operation, told BBC News NI: "They were two very lucky people." It is believed the pair are originally from overseas but live in Ireland and were on a visit to Achill Island, off the County Mayo coast, when the incident happened.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: McManamon said the couple had gone for a walk along Keel Beach when the tide began to come in behind them - at one point reaching above knee-level.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "They got engaged in Achill and they were just walking along [the beach] and they went out too far on the rocks," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "The weather conditions were atrocious there, and in that particular area the tide has come in very quick." Unable to get off the sand because of the towering cliff behind them, the couple called 999 and asked for a coast guard rescue.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "It was too rough for a rib (rigid inflatable boat) to be tasked - it was blowing Force 8 to 10 at the time and the wave conditions wouldn't let us," McManamon said.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "When the helicopter came, they tried to move in to winch them but there was too much down draft off the mountain for it to happen," McManamon explained.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: So he then deployed climbers from Achill Island Coast Guard's cliff rescue team who abseiled down the cliff to pluck the couple out of the rising tide.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "The water was coming in around them - the water was roughly just above their knees," McManamon recalled.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: The couple were taken to safety in stages.
sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.article_title: Dramatic clifftop rescue of bride and groom-to-be

sentences.text: "It can be a dangerous spot, the locals don't really go near it at all," he said, explaining that other parts of the beach are more suitable for walking or swimming.

sentences.text: The Rothbury Estate, in Northumberland, covers a swathe of woodland and farmland Conservationists have completed the purchase of a huge upland estate following a two-year £30m public appeal backed by the likes of Sir David Attenborough.
sentences.article_title: Attenborough-backed appeal secures £30m estate

sentences.text: The Wildlife Trusts - a federation of 47 conservation charities - and Northumberland Wildlife Trust (NWT) plan to "enhance the rich natural heritage" of the Rothbury Estate, a 9,500-acre stretch of former grouse moor, woodland and farmland - having headed off fears it could be split among multiple owners.

sentences.text: Broadcaster Sir David described it as an opportunity "to create something very special for generations to come".

sentences.article_title: Attenborough-backed appeal secures £30m estate

sentences.text: Worried public access could become more difficult if it was divided between owners, the wildlife organisations bought an initial tract in 2024 covering the Simonside Hills and a mixture of lowland, woods, riverside and farmland.

sentences.text: Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons.

sentences.text: Doran's sister messaged back: "I'm not tearing up… YOU'RE tearing up." News of a video game remake bought back happy memories for Kacey Doran This is the power of nostalgia – and a perfect example of how video games can trigger it.

sentences.article_title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia

sentences.text: Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the UK's most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The 57-year old is the first Black person to oversee the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The City of London Corporation is an administrative body with responsibility for London's central financial district, headed by its own Lord Mayor.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas tops the 2027 Black Powerlist, which recognises the most powerful people of African and Caribbean heritage in the UK.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The award body said he was "a respected public-service leader with over 30 years' experience in local government".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Other influential names in this year's top ten include entrepreneurs Emma Grede and Steven Bartlett, as well as actor and filmmaker Sir Idris Elba.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Comedian Sir Lenny Henry has also been recognised, with a Lifetime Achievement award, for co-founding Comic Relief, which has raised over £1.6bn since 1985.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Now in its 21st year, the Black Powerlist celebrates people who have broken through barriers to reach leadership roles, thereby inspiring future generations.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "It exists to show young people of African and Caribbean heritage what is possible, in fields they might never have considered," said Michael Eboda, the list's publisher.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: As chief executive, he oversees around 5,000 staff with responsibilities including the City of London Police, 11,000 acres of open spaces such as Epping Forest and Hampstead Heath, and advocacy for the UK's financial and professional services sector.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Thomas was born in Sheffield to parents who made the city their home after leaving Jamaica as part of the Windrush generation.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: "They worked incredibly hard and instilled that sense of discipline and respect, and that's the core of how I do business," he said of his upbringing.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Growing up, Thomas aspired to be a footballer and took part in trials alongside Alan Shearer.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Reflecting on his own change of direction, Thomas joked it was about "following dreams and if they don't come true… there's always something else".
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: Before joining the City of London Corporation, Thomas served as chief executive of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames where he oversaw public services and a £1.2bn regeneration programme.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: He was appointed a CBE in the 2019 New Year Honours in the wake of the Rotherham Abuse scandal for transforming children's services during his time as strategic director for children and young people at Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council.
sentences.article_title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist

sentences.text: The US Federal Reserve has held interest rates steady at 3.75% - 4%.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The decision comes within a week of the midterm elections and after the central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years at its September meeting.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: "The overwhelming consensus, the overwhelming judgement, is that what we've done in this monetary medicine is starting to work some," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said, referring to September's interest rate rise.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Figures published after the Fed's announcement showed the US economy growing at a stronger pace than expected, with inflation running above the Fed's target.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: An interest rate tells people and businesses how much it costs to borrow money – such as with credit cards, mortgages, or business loans – but also what return they get for saving cash.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed influences interest rates in the US through its target range for the federal funds rate, which is the interest rate used by commercial banks for overnight borrowing.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: In its decision to hold rates steady this month, the Fed said that while inflation remains high, it wanted to gather more information before making another decision to change rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed also noted that while there was uncertainty, the US economy remained resilient.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Warsh acknowledged that inflation remained too high, but noted that there were other signs - such as tightening credit conditions - that the economy was moving in the right direction.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: There is plenty more economic data to come between now and the committee's next meeting, the Fed chair added, which should paint a more detailed picture of the state of the economy.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: At that point, Warsh said, "we'll be, I think, better positioned to determine the right policy decision and the stance of policy." While last month the committee signalled there could be one more rate rise this year, Warsh would not be drawn out on where he thinks they will go in six weeks' time.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: "A lot of things can happen, so I'm not going to be able to share with you my musings." The decision to hold rates steady was not unanimous.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: While 10 of the 12 committee members voted to keep rates unchanged, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voted to increase rates to 4%-4.25%, from its current 3.75%-4%.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The bank's next meeting will be held over 8-9 December.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Warsh said things are moving in the right direction, while the US economy is performing very strongly.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The US economy grew by 3.4% on an annualised basis in the three months to September, stronger than analysts had expected.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: That strong growth was driven by an acceleration in investment, and strong consumer spending.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: While there was an annualised increase in personal spending of 3.8%, the annualised increase in private investment was a huge 19.4% which analysts say was largely due to investment in artificial intelligence.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Inflation is also above the Fed's target range.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Prices increased by 3.7% in the year to September, driven higher by fuel and energy prices which have surged off the back of the war in Iran.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed uses interest rate changes to try to keep inflation – the rate at which prices change – at 2% a year and keep the job market stable.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: When inflation is too high, the Fed tends to raise interest rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: This tends to mean higher rates from banks and other lenders, which in turn affects spending and saving decisions.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: For example, someone refinancing their mortgage or buying a property for the first time could face higher mortgage rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It could also mean higher interest rates on credit cards or car loans.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: However, it means higher interest rates on savings as well.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: This encourages people and businesses to save more, spend less money, and make less investments.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It also encourages companies to hire less people or slow the pace of pay rises.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: All of this tends to reduce demand and slow inflation.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: When inflation is low or if the Fed believes the economy needs a boost, it cut rates.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The idea is that this will have the opposite affect, with banks dropping rates leading to more spending and less saving from people and businesses.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: Leaving the rates unchanged means rates on things like new mortgages or business loans are also less likely to change.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: It also means interest rates on cash savings are unlikely to rise.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: US interest rates have historically moved around quite a bit.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The last time Fed rates were as high as they have been recently was in the lead up to and during the start of the 2008 global financial crisis.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: The Fed then dropped rates to historic lows to encourage spending and job creation during the economic slump and kept them at those lows for several years.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: They picked up again ahead of the pandemic before dropping to as low as 0%-0.25% during the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: They then rose to highs of 5.25%-5% from the middle of 2023 to August 2024 as inflation jumped.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: They had been falling steadily since then, until rates were raised last month.
sentences.article_title: US interest rates held steady and economy grows - what it means for you

sentences.text: People are facing a "painful" and "depressing" few years ahead, economic think tanks have warned, after forecasts showed growth in living standards grinding almost to a halt.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Typical working-age households would see their disposable income fall by £1,050, or 3%, between now and 2029, according to the Resolution Foundation, while the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the current decade would be the worst for household income growth on record.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey said his Budget offered "breathing space", but said the government could "never remove completely" cost of living pressures.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The UK's official forecaster said its latest economic forecast painted a "pretty grim picture".
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), blamed the difficult financial situation facing the UK on higher borrowing costs and inflation caused by the US-Iran war.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: In response to rising energy prices, Healey has announced measures, including a £100 support payment, aimed at easing pressure on household finances.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: While the Resolution Foundation focused its forecast for living standards on working age households, the OBR looks at all households, including pensioners and reflects a 10-year rolling average growth to take into account short-term fluctuations.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: "This decade looks set to be the worst decade for growth in household incomes on record," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Painful' years ahead, think tanks warn, as living standards set to fall

sentences.text: Bereaved families will no longer be hit by an unexpected tax bill because of severe delays paying out civil service pensions, following a change in Wednesday's Budget.

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Crime scene evidence is often not enough to identify suspects Randy Gail Sperino was last seen alive on the evening of 9 November 1993, as she was getting into a pickup truck in Granite City, Illinois.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The 34-year-old's body was found hours later in a field nearby, the victim of blunt force trauma.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The identity of her killer was a mystery.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: DNA evidence found at the crime scene was tested against standard law enforcement databases, but no matches were found.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: For three decades, investigators from the Madison County Sheriff's Office chased leads and interviewed hundreds of people as they attempted to identify the perpetrator.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The case looked like it would remain one of more than 250,000 unsolved homicides in the US.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Then, last year, detectives tried a fresh approach.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They sent genetic evidence to Othram, a Houston-based company that uses DNA technology to help identify the perpetrators in cold and current crime cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Madison County detectives had been inspired by investigative genetic genealogy techniques used to identify the Golden State Killer, Joseph James DeAngelo, back in 2018.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: In that case, an investigative team constructed a family tree to help identify the killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They were able to do so thanks to DNA data that relatives had provided to commercial databases, similar to consumer ancestry platforms.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Unlike traditional forensic DNA testing, which generally relies on a direct comparison between evidence and a known person, investigative genetic genealogy can identify distant genetic relatives of an unknown individual.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram set about applying this technique to track down Sperino's killer.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While the suspect's own DNA profile wasn't available, profiles submitted by his extended relatives allowed the company to identify a male family member.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "That lead broke the case open," said Captain Tim Lawrence of Madison County Sheriff's Office, which was responsible for investigating the crime.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It was a crucial clue that led the detectives to Albert "Buddy" Zigler, 70, who police say then confessed to the murder.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: He was charged in May this year.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Wes Sperino, Gail's son, said at a press conference: "I finally get closure and I finally know who did this." Albert Zigler was charged with murder in May The technique that led detectives to Zigler is credited with revolutionising how forensic cases are solved.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: It has been highly successful in helping solve cases involving unidentified human remains and identifying suspects in longstanding investigations.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram claims it has helped solve thousands of cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: However, Mittelman is quick to point out that DNA technology can only go so far before "a cascade of investigative steps" are needed.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: An Othram scientist prepares a bone for DNA extraction DNA science isn't the only technology that is helping detectives solve cold cases.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: One of the challenges facing detectives on major investigations like the hunt for Sperino's attacker is the sheer amount of evidence they dig up.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Officers investigating her murder realised AI could help them wade through the mountains of evidence they had accumulated since 1993.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: They used a platform called Centerline AI, from Florida software company CentralSquare, to analyse more than 2,000 pages of records and identify evidence for the DNA testing that helped to break the case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The AI helped them reconstruct timelines and organise witness information.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "It's so much easier than having a detective have to read through 2,000 pages," Lawrence says.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: His team could interact with the AI like a chat bot.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: This also helped when it came to interviewing Zigler after they had tracked him down.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Detectives were able to ask questions of the AI to help "figure out if Zigler was being truthful", says Lawrence.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: But the technology is "only as good as the investigator," says the captain.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: There comes a point, he says, "where you leave the technology behind and you have to go track people down and talk to them." Investigative genetic genealogy has its limitations too.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Mittelman says: "It can't solve every case.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: If you have no DNA, you can't really use this technique." "But this technique is a lot more powerful and a lot more likely to yield identities than having to rely on the chance that you find a match somewhere in a database," he adds.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While firms like Othram only use ancestry platforms where users have provided consent for law enforcement matching, there remain some concerns about the ethical implications of using this data.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "There are significant privacy concerns," says Denise Syndercombe Court, professor of forensic genetics at King's College London.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While one person may have opted in to their DNA being used, genetic relatives may not have given consent.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: A lack of funding is another hurdle.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Mittelman says: "Every law enforcement agency wants to do it.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: There's just not a lot of funding for it." Sometimes cases are funded through donations or crowdfunding.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: Othram operates a website listing cases that members of the public can help fund.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: While investigative genetic genealogy has been adopted in countries such as Sweden, Denmark and Australia, it is not yet used in the UK.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The Home Office is conducting a study to consider whether it should be adopted in the UK but did not respond to a request for comment.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: The UK is already in a strong position, says Syndercombe Court.
sentences.article_title: The tech helping crack decades-old cold cases

sentences.text: "We have such an efficient DNA database that if you can get any DNA out of a crime scene, you've got over a 65% chance of putting a name to that person, which is enormously powerful," she says.

sentences.text: Mohammed Ashim is paid to film his hands at work Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working." He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off." But his customers are getting more demanding.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people." And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Shahil Baig expects dozens more firms to start collecting video of workers Why is such data so important?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: And until recently, that data was not available.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US." This video can not be played The factory workers teaching robots how to work like humans But are workers collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs?
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: At the moment it's too early to tell says Bino Paul, senior professor at the School of Management and Labour Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) in Mumbai.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: For some workers AI might be a useful tool, but robots could automate other jobs, he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: The problem is that, if machines do start to take over, there will be little workers can do about.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "By the time workers realise what they have participated in, things may have gone too far," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Like many others, he wants governments to regulate AI.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "AI cannot be viewed merely as a technical system.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: We need to develop a socio-technical system in which ethics is upheld through human agency, ensuring that AI delivers beneficence rather than maleficence." Despite concerns over where AI is heading, money is still being poured into its development.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Some of that trickles down to workers in India, where there is no shortage of workers prepared to wear a camera for a few dollars a day.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Mohammed Arman has been working in the textiles industry in Bangalore for 10 years.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: "Garments stitching and cutting.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: I know this work so well I could probably do it with my eyes closed.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: Cloth, thread, needle, machine after 10 years, your hands just know what to do before your mind even tells them," he says.
sentences.article_title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI

sentences.text: He has recently started wearing a head-mounted camera that records his work.

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.

sentences.text: Newquay Mayor Drew Creek said he could not stand by the Greens' Zionism is racism motion The leader of the Green Party on Cornwall Council has defected following the party's recent "Zionism is racism" motion.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Drew Creek joined the Labour and Co-operatives on Thursday after the policy motion was passed at the Green Party's conference earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Creek, who is Mayor of Newquay and serves as a councillor for Trenance ward, said he had "huge respect" for Greens across Cornwall but the motion "crossed a line".
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: The Cornwall Green Party said it was "deeply saddened" by Creek's decision to join Labour and said it does not "try to impose uniformity of belief" among its members and elected representatives.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: More news stories for Cornwall Listen to the latest news for Cornwall The motion backed by Green members at its party conference said Zionism was an ideology supporting "an ethnonationalist Jewish state in historic Palestine to the exclusion and/or domination of the non-Jewish population".
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: It has been criticised by Jewish groups , as well as some Green MPs and opposition political parties .
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Creek said he hoped the Green Party would step back from the stance – but said instead, "Zack Polanski and the leadership has doubled down".
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: "I can't stand behind that, and I won't pretend otherwise," the councillor said.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: He added: "People in Newquay don't want politicians driving division.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: They want someone who'll fix the roads, protect our coast, fight for local services and bring people together.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: "That's the kind of politics I believe in and the kind of politics Andy Burnham has shown.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Zack Polanski previously said he would not overturn the motion "Newquay is my home and where I am raising my family.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: I came into politics for one reason, to stand up for this town and the people in it.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Labour is where I believe I can do that best, and I'm looking forward to getting on with the job." Councillor Kate Ewert, Labour and Co-operative Group Leader on Cornwall Council said Creek's decision "highlights the serious questions about Zack Polanski's leadership".
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: Noah Law, MP for St Austell and Newquay, added: "In this period of polarised politics, it takes great courage to stand up for what you believe in.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: They said: "Disagreements over the wording of this one motion should not distract from the fact that the Green Party is united in its condemnation of the racist genocide and ethnic cleansing that Israel is perpetrating in Gaza and the occupied territories, and united in its demand for much tougher sanctions on Israel.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: "Labour, by contrast, refuses even to recognise that what we are seeing is genocide, and continues to allow arms exports to and intelligence-sharing with the government that is committing it.
sentences.article_title: Mayor defects from Greens after Zionism motion

sentences.text: "It's hard to see how anyone who is serious about action on climate, action to end extreme inequality, and action to prevent an ongoing genocide could switch their support to a party that is not serious about any of these." sentences.text: Andy Burnham has said he wants to cut the welfare bill "as soon as we possibly can", but was unable to guarantee this would happen before the next general election.

sentences.text: Asked whether he would seek to reduce the bill before the next election, Burnham told reporters: "We want to get the welfare bill down as quickly as possible, and we're working flat out to that end." He warned against "crude cuts" and said he wants to get people into "sustainable employment".

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey and Prime Minister Andy Burnham have both spoken of their desire for the benefits bill to come down, but the government has not yet laid out a timetable for any reductions.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Their political opponents have criticised them for a lack of detail on welfare reform in Wednesday's Budget, accusing the government of delaying difficult decisions over cuts.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: BBC Verify has taken a look at the numbers behind this thorny political issue and some of the difficult options the government have to bring down welfare costs.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The official forecaster, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR), estimates in its latest forecasts that the cost of the welfare system will rise , external from £353bn this year to £431bn in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The OBR's figures include spending on pensioners, which accounts for just under half of the total.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: The majority of this cost is on the state pension.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, if we look at the size of welfare spending relative to the size of the overall economy the OBR's projections are less dramatic, increasing from 11.1% today to 11.3% of GDP in 2032.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Total welfare spending would also remain below the peak of around 12% of GDP in 2013 following the global financial crisis, leading some economists and researchers to question the idea that welfare spending is out of control. , external But there are some welfare costs that are rising rapidly.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Spending on health and disability related benefits, in particular Personal Independence Payments (PIP), is up sharply since the Covid-19 pandemic.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Accounting for inflation, spending on working-age disability benefits increased from £14bn in 2020 to £25bn in 2026 , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Inflation-adjusted welfare spending remains lower than 2013 because several other working-age benefits, such as Universal Credit and housing benefit, were cut by Conservative-led governments as part of their austerity programme from 2010 onwards , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: So spending in some parts of the system has come down while it has risen in others - and there could be a connection.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Some researchers think the post-2010 welfare cuts to benefits might have created an incentive for people to claim sickness and disability benefits instead to protect their living standards , external , therefore shifting costs around the system rather than generating lasting savings.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Many also see a specific problem regarding the growing number of young people in the welfare system claiming benefits, including PIP.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Official figures show the number of 16 to 24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training (Neets) has risen , external by around 230,000 since 2019 to just under one million.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Former Labour health secretary Alan Milburn is leading an official review into Neets and is expected to recommend major reforms designed to get many off benefits and into work.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: His interim report in May estimated that annual PIP expenditure on 16 to 24-year-olds rose from £1.3bn in 2020 to around £3.2bn in 2025 , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: It also projected this cost would reach £6.5bn and cover 700,000 young people in five years' time.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: PIP claimants can be in work, but official statistics show that only around one in five are , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: Politicians are often unclear about what they mean by reducing spending on welfare.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: In March 2025, former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer's government presented a plan which it said would save £5bn a year from health-related welfare spending by 2030 by tightening PIP access and reducing the value of health-related Universal Credit payments.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: But official forecasts made it clear that annual spending on health-related welfare in cash terms was still set to rise after the reform , external , just not as rapidly as the path it had previously been on.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: However, at the time the OBR did forecast the plans would help put overall UK welfare spending on a "slightly downward trajectory" as a share of the economy , external over the medium term, rather than remaining flat as had been previously projected.
sentences.article_title: What are the government's options for reducing welfare spending?

sentences.text: So this type of relative reduction in anticipated welfare spending, rather than a cut in absolute cash terms, could be what the government seeks to deliver.

sentences.text: There are also suggestions Timms could propose a new PIP eligibility test to reduce access , external , although he was not specifically instructed to find savings.

sentences.text: But some analysts argue that to be effective in delivering sustainable savings, such reforms are likely also to require the government to spend a lot more , external to enable young people in particular to get into and remain in work.

sentences.text: Andy Burnham and Rhun ap Iorwerth met in Glasgow on Friday Welsh First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth says there has been a "significant step forward" with regards to his country's spending and borrowing powers after meeting the prime minister.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Andy Burnham held a meeting of his National Economic Council with the first ministers of Wales and Scotland on Friday, after which ap Iorwerth said it was a matter of "how and when" a loosening of financial restrictions will take place.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: At the summit in Glasgow, Burnham lobbied the government leaders to devolve "deeper" to the regions of Wales and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: The prime minister said the two first ministers had agreed to work with him on "regional empowerment".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: No timescales were announced for changes to Wales' finances.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Friday's meeting followed rows between the Welsh and UK government over the chancellor's Budget on Wednesday, which ap Iorwerth had said was "not serious about Wales".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: His party Plaid Cymru said the budget left the Welsh government with a real-terms cut in funding, which the UK government denied.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Rhun ap Iorwerth, John Swinney, joined by Welsh Finance Minister Elin Jones, attended the meeting on Friday Ap Iorwerth had set out a range of demands to the prime minister in a letter sent at the start of October.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: As well as calling for powers over policing and justice, and for more funding for rail projects, he called for an end to restrictions on access to the Wales reserve - spare funding that the Welsh government can store in one year to use in another.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: It is capped at £385m, and the Welsh government can only draw down £137.5m and £55m for resource and capital spend respectively per year.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: The Welsh government can also borrow up to £1.1bn for infrastructure, with a limit of £165m a year.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth said: "There were some real positives here.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "On fiscal flexibility, the ability for us to use our funding better in Wales, use our reserves better in Wales - and on borrowing powers, I was told clearly that its now was a matter of how and when.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: That is a significant step forward." He said there was "clearly an interest" for the prime minister to "really understand that sheer injustice of underfunding of rail in Wales that we have seen for many years".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "That is a particular issue we will be taking forward now between my office and his," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: On policing, the first minister said "I think instinctively the prime minister wants to go there and there's still work to do".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: At a speech this month the first minister called for "practical agreement" on how the two governments could work together on the economy, calling for Westminster to avoid duplication in areas that are devolved already to the Welsh government.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Burnham said Friday's meeting was "positive", and that both first ministers had agreed to "work together jointly on regional empowerment in Scotland and Wales as well".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "We now have a process where we have detailed work by officials on both sides to see if we can come to a set of arrangements that are right for Scotland and right for Wales," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "We had a good discussion today on two fronts, one around re-industrialisation and the offer of more devolution of innovation funding to the regional level." He said it was for Scotland and Wales to decide how that looks.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Burnham also said the UK government will now look at arrangements for further devolution of employment support.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock fiscal flexibilities and borrowing was on the agenda for future Welsh government discussions with No 10 North.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "It is going to take some conversations on how that would work in practice.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "I can't give you a specific time frame as things stand," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Following Wednesday's Budget, which saw an extra £450m announced for Wales over the next three years as well as funding for individual projects, the Welsh government claimed the extra money would represent a real-terms cut to its own finances.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: A £30m funding pledge for a new railway station in Cardiff was also described as "an insult" by Wales' transport minister.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: On Radio Wales Breakfast on Friday before the summit, ap Iorwerth said there were "paltry sums of money coming on rail, when they've said there's £14bn on the way" and a "real terms cut in the money we have to spend on public services".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "The Budget was not serious about Wales," he said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: He said in another interview he could "only assume that the prime minister is holding something back".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth told BBC Wales that Wednesday's Budget had "so little mention" of his nation After the meeting, Downing Street said ap Iorwerth had "agreed to start a process to explore how each government could contribute to regional empowerment, reindustrialisation and achieving good growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "This would be a policy sprint led by No 10 North, involving officials from each government, to take this agenda forward," they said.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Ap Iorwerth said in a statement: "There was an encouraging consensus that the fiscal and borrowing powers which have for so long put Wales at a disadvantage compared with other UK nations must be revised as a matter of urgency.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: "I welcome the prime minister's comments that this is now a matter of how and when." Welsh ministers had called for changes to their borrowing rules and assurances that child poverty payments it wants to introduce would leave recipients' tax and benefits allowances unaffected.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: None of that was addressed in the Budget, although Welsh Secretary Stephen Kinnock has said "positive" talks were continuing regarding the child poverty payments.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Friday's meeting of the National Economic Council - a summit to help boost the UK economy - was due to be attended by the prime minister and all the devolved leaders.
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: However, it emerged on Thursday that Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill would not be there after her attendance was blocked by her Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).
sentences.article_title: First minister says Welsh spending powers takes step forward after Andy Burnham meeting

sentences.text: Since he became prime minister, Burnham has consistently spoken in favour of devolution.
