sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Parliament's live broadcast showed the moments surrounding the alleged incident A war of words has broken out between Lib Dem MP Caroline Voaden and Reform UK leader Nigel Farage over an alleged physical altercation in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The row was triggered when Farage, explaining why he had not attended Wednesday's Budget, said he had been involved in a "physical altercation" with another MP at the State Opening of Parliament in May and had wanted to avoid a similar incident.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: Voaden revealed herself to be the MP Farage had been referring to, writing on social media that she had been left "shocked and bloody angry" by the confrontation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The Lib Dems have claimed that Farage "attempted to shove" their South Devon MP but a Reform source accused the party of "lying".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The Reform insider added: "The Lib Dems were claiming Nigel shoved her and that she was shaken, the video disproves that clearly." Footage, first unearthed by the Daily Telegraph, shows the pair leaving the chamber together at the state opening of Parliament but there is no visible evidence of a major altercation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: However, Voaden has said the incident between herself and Farage was not shown in the clip originally posted by the Telegraph , external .
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The incident does not appear to have been captured on the official feed of the state opening provided by Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: Voaden said Farage had been ordered to apologise to her after she complained to Commons authorities.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: The House of Commons would not comment on this.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: In a statement, Voaden said: "The truth is that on the day of the King's Speech, Farage missed his chance to process with the other party leaders to the Lords, and rather than queue with the rest of us, he shoved me out of the way to barge past.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: "Such behaviour is unacceptable in any workplace, and it has no place in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: In response he said: "At the State Opening of Parliament, I got involved… I didn't want to… but I got involved in a physical altercation with an MP in the chamber.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: "I didn't make a fuss about it, I didn't complain, but I could see given that my prayer card had been removed, I was heading towards another physical altercation.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems and Reform UK in war of words over alleged shove

sentences.text: A spokesperson for the House of Commons said that a prayer card for Farage - the way in which MPs reserve seats in the Commons - did not "display a valid date stamp" and therefore "was removed in line with the usual Chamber protocol".

sentences.text: Local government minister Jim McMahon has announced plans in five areas will go ahead The government has announced further delays to nine of 14 major council mergers, with only five now going ahead.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Proposals for 14 regions to undergo mergers of smaller councils to form larger unitary authorities was put on hold by Local Government Secretary Angela Rayner last month, following concerns around legal challenges.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Local Government Minister Jim McMahon has told MPs the review had found the government's decision-making to be "robust", but nine areas have now been withdrawn for further review.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Only five of the original 14 regions will be taken forward, after three more weeks of consultation.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Shadow local government secretary Katie Lam condemned the latest news as "a farce".
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Mergers will continue to progress in East Sussex, Gloucestershire, Oxfordshire , Warwickshire and Worcestershire .
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: But the government is seeking "legal clarity" in the remaining nine areas, which are: Derbyshire , Devon , Hertfordshire , Kent, Lancashire, Leicestershire , Lincolnshire , Nottinghamshire , and Staffordshire.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: In a Commons statement, McMahon said the government was "withdrawing the decisions announced in July" for those nine areas.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: "I want to be absolutely clear that this is not a reflection of the work underpinning those proposals," he added.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: The review will now focus on the nine areas where current plans have been withdrawn for further review, as well as four areas where plans were withdrawn in September, in Essex , Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Two further areas, Cambridgeshire and West Sussex, are still waiting for merger plans to be agreed, totalling 15 regions where local government reorganisation plans remain undecided.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: McMahon said: "We will move faster where we can, and some of the remaining areas may receive an outcome decision before others.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: Responding, Lam set out how the reorganisation had been beset by delays over the past two-and-a-half years.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: "From start to finish this government's approach to local government reorganisation has been nothing short of a farce," she told MPs.
sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: She added: "Naturally the taxpayer was left to pick up the tab for all of these delays - a bill which runs into the tens of millions of pounds." Local Government Association chair Eamonn O'Brien called for a re-set of relations between the government and local councils across the country.

sentences.article_title: Further delays for major council overhaul in nine of 14 proposed areas

sentences.text: "All councils affected need urgent clarity on next steps and how costs already incurred will be met.

sentences.text: Tony Vaughan (pictured) has shown remorse, according to a report A Labour MP has said sorry in the House of Commons following complaints over his behaviour towards a female member of staff.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: It comes as the Independent Expert Panel published a report , external requiring Tony Vaughan to apologise for breaching Parliament's bullying and harassment policy.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The MP for Folkestone and Hythe was found by the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards to have committed the breach after a constituency staff member complained he "behaved towards [her] in an overbearing and belittling manner".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan said on Thursday he accepted the findings in full.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "As a result of these behaviours, my former colleague was upset and humiliated," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "My behaviour had a real and continuing impact on her and her family, and I am truly sorry for this." The Labour Party said it "expects the highest standards of conduct from all our members and elected representatives.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "We have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "It is right that Tony Vaughan has apologised following this independent process," a spokesperson added.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan, who has represented his Kent constituency since 2024, was found to have hugged the complainant without consent at an office event.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: He also took her personal mobile phone from her hand to join an online meeting without asking permission and failed to explain why phone calls between them had ended abruptly.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: Vaughan appealed the Commissioner's findings, though the Independent Expert Panel confirmed the majority of them, according to Parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The sub-panel stressed that "oppressive and bullying behaviour towards [MPs'] staff members is wholly unacceptable".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: It added that Vaughan's actions were breaches of "basic boundaries and courtesy" - rather than failures in management - and an "abuse of his power".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: MP apologises over bullying and harassment The politician told MPs on Thursday that he was not "sufficiently alert" to the power imbalances between him and his employee.

sentences.text: He added he recognised his behaviour could well impact on "someone who is vulnerable whether or not that is known".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "I made mistakes," Vaughan continued.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The 36-page report said it took account of the impact of what happened on the complainant, who has a right to anonymity.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: She said she was left feeling stressed, exhausted and offended, it adds.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: The report also stated that Vaughan had "expressed genuine and thoughtful remorse".
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: He should be required to make an "unreserved apology" to the complainant and the House by way of a personal statement in the House of Commons Chamber, it continued.
sentences.article_title: MP apologises over bullying and harassment

sentences.text: "We consider that this achieves the appropriate balance and clear messaging required regarding the behaviour expected of MPs," the report said.

sentences.text: Vaughan added he had undertaken further training as a result of the incident.

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey unveiled his Budget on Wednesday This was a Budget I would describe as a flotilla of small measures.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Westminster is poring over the 150 page Red Book , external in which the Budget is printed and also what is formally called the Economic and Fiscal Outlook published , external by the watchdog and forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility, the OBR.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: The Red Book sets out the measures the chancellor will implement and how much they will cost.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: There are 98 of them, considerably more than normal and more than in either of Rachel Reeves' budgets.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: But nearly all of them are pretty small in terms of their impact on the Treasury's spreadsheets.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: This gets to the heart of why those involved in compiling this Budget have been irritated by commentary in the build up to it suggesting there would be nothing to see in John Healey's address – but also why those suggesting that were arguably onto something as well.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Firstly, as expected, it was a much smaller Budget in overall tax and spending terms than plenty of recent ones have been.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: But there were plenty of measures here and there which the chancellor will hope enough people notice and value – and others that some will likely curse.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: There are more taxes for savers and landlords, for instance, and too for banks.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: When a government has promised, as Labour have, to not put up income tax, national insurance or VAT – the big revenue generators – they end up looking elsewhere if they conclude putting up tax is necessary.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: That runs the political risk of choosing particular sectors who might respond rather noisily.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Think of the plenty of farmers who were incensed by the changes to inheritance tax Rachel Reeves was keen on.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: And there is a recurring sense of déjà vu in the language of the OBR.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: "The UK's economic and fiscal position remains very challenging," it says, with a splash of understatement, adding that "there have been further adverse developments" this year with in the conflict in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: As for what happens, next, well, frankly, who on earth knows.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: What happens, for instance, in the Middle East, once the mid term elections are done in America and the result of the Israeli general election is clear?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: In short, the chancellor felt constrained in his capacity to act and his capacity to make a noticeable positive difference is perhaps constrained even more so – because any intervention, even expensive ones, may merely make a grim situation a bit less bad , rather than things actually feeling better.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Mitigating the bad is arguably a noble political aim, but it costs money and potentially comes with little political upside.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: This video can not be played What are the standout points from the Budget?
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Instead there is this fleet of smaller measures that the government will hope gives their MPs something to try to sell – while acknowledging that they are not world changing.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Luke Tryl, the UK Director of the More in Common think tank, says: "The softly populist tone of this budget is likely to land well with the public.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: "Instead, by offering support to all of those on Council Tax bands A to D, he is able to reassure them that the government will support them too." The reaction of the opposition parties, from a range of different political perspectives, amounts to a critique that this Budget was thin.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: In summary, this felt like a cautious Budget.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: One critical friend of the government suggested to me this would be a "Mr Sensible Budget" – their hope and expectation that it might be shorn of bells and whistles, but shorn of timebombs too.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Budget felt cautious despite its range of small measures

sentences.text: Prime Minister's Questions focused on Andy Burnham's Brexit stance Andy Burnham has insisted there is "no confusion" over his position on the European Union, as he criticised the UK's current deal with the bloc.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: The prime minister said it was his "responsibility" to improve the deal, which was ratified in 2020, at a summit in Brussels next month.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: He denied he had shifted his stance since the Makerfield by-election when he promised not to "re-run" the Brexit debate .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Earlier this week, he suggested he could call a referendum on the UK returning to EU freedom of movement, before No10 appeared to backtrack .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch accused him during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday of failing to "respect" the 2016 Brexit vote.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Badenoch said Burnham had created confusion and asked if he wanted a referendum on rejoining the EU.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "There is no confusion at all," Burnham told MPs.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "The government has a collectively agreed position, which I have set out today.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It is entirely consistent with everything that I've said, including in the by-election.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "The red lines in our manifesto, including on freedom of movement, will stay in place firmly for the whole of this Parliament." Labour's 2024 election manifesto ruled out a return of free movement, single market membership or a customs union.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Freedom of movement allows EU citizens to travel, live, study and work in any member country.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: It is a precondition of membership of the EU's single market, which enables goods, services and people to move freely between EU member states.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Badenoch accused Burnham of having "opened his mouth without engaging his brain" over freedom of movement during "the chancellor's big week" as the Budget is unveiled .
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It was miserable, regardless of which side of the debate you were on." Burnham said Badenoch was "speaking the truth" here and the country had suffered from low growth and insufficient control on migration as a result of a "harder Brexit than what was promised" in the 2016 referendum.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Where I am focused is getting a better deal for Britain, that is my responsibility, and I will lead from this despatch box over the next few weeks," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: At a summit in Brussels on 20 November, Burnham will push options for a reset of relations with the bloc on issues such as youth mobility, food, drink, energy and cooperation on illegal immigration.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: Burnham's comments at Prime Minister's Questions came as a letter emerged addressed to his Cabinet ministers, asking them to be "aligned and disciplined" around the summit.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "It will not be appropriate for ministers individually to advocate for specific options or opine on the likely outcome of the process," he wrote in a letter on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: He said he hoped the summit led to "some important, concrete steps" and he would set out the next steps "to consider the UK's long-term relationship with the EU as part of our 10-year plan".
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Both the UK and the EU have changed considerably in the 10 years since the Brexit vote," he said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.text: "Any future relationship depends on practical arrangements that are realistic for both sides, and responsive to this new reality." Any "fundamental change" to this relationship "would be for the public to decide and a matter for the next Parliament," he added.
sentences.article_title: Burnham insists 'no confusion at all' over his Brexit position

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: While her symptoms are not directly linked to vitamin D deficiency - she realised something was wrong.

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: In the UK, low vitamin D rates are increasing in some age groups , external - particularly in girls and young women.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: According to data from the National Diet and Nutrition Survey, last year nearly a quarter of 11- to 18-year-olds were classed as deficient.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D can come from our diet, in foods such as oily fish and meat, or supplements.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: But most is made by our body when UV light in sunlight hits the skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Covering parts of the body and wearing sunscreen also has an impact - despite their protective advantages.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Those with darker skin need exposure to stronger light to produce the same amount of vitamin D as lighter skin.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Vitamin D deficiency is linked to the bone disease rickets in babies and infants.
sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

Amaka Osu says she doesn't think many of her friends realise what the symptoms are Amaka was in the middle of making dinner at her university house in Liverpool when she started shaking.

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.article_title: I didn't know I was lacking in vitamin D until I collapsed at work

sentences.text: Mindy says people often presume she is straight because of her age As a 75-year-old lesbian, Mindy Meleyal has lived through every major milestone in the modern LGBT rights movement, from the start of decriminalisation in 1967 to the first same-sex marriages in 2014.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: But now she says this important part of her identity is frequently overlooked due to her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She's part of England's older LGBTQ+ community, which a new report suggests often experiences poorer health, more limited finances and greater social isolation than the wider older population.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report, from the Centre for Ageing Better, says without specialist support, this growing demographic could be forced "back into the closet" when accessing care, warning they may even delay getting the care they need because of concerns about homophobia.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Adam Preston, a housing development manager from the LGBT Foundation charity, says he regularly meets older members of the community in exactly that situation.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "It's very common for people to hide things if they have a carer visiting their home, for example hiding their wedding photos or taking down a trans flag," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston is part of the team behind Kindred House, a first-of-its-kind LGBTQ+ social housing scheme for over-55s, set to open in Manchester next year.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: An artist's impression of what Kindred House will look like when it opens The scheme, a joint project with the local council, will provide 80 self-contained apartments and communal areas available to the local community.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The majority of residents will be LGBTQ+.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Kindred House scheme is what's known as extra-care housing, which means residents live independently, but there is a 24/7 care team available for those who need extra help, and all staff will receive specialist training around LGBTQ+ inclusion.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Preston says he hopes the scheme will "trigger some conversations" about how to best support older LGBTQ+ people in the challenges they face.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Mindy and her wife Linda have been together for more than 30 years, but says they're often mistaken for sisters.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "She's 18 inches taller than me, I've got a Yorkshire accent and she's got a Northern Irish accent," Mindy says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "I think it's pretty obvious we weren't brought up in the same building." She believes part of that is often down to people presuming she is straight because of her age.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "There are different tribes of people in every age group, but when you get older, people start clumping you together with other stereotypes," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: After divorcing her husband and coming out as lesbian, Mindy co-founded a lesbian commune in Hull before moving to Manchester On one occasion, while Mindy was in hospital after a stroke, a nurse referred to Linda as Mindy's husband.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: She said it was not only "insulting", but made her consider what sort of training the staff might have had.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The Spotlight on Ageing report says these sort of experiences can also have an impact on the support people receive.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Sarah Wilkinson, research and analysis manager at the Centre for Ageing Better, says after a "lifetime of homophobia and transphobia", older LGBTQ+ people now face the "additional, and overlapping, challenge of ageism".
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report , external says older LGBTQ+ people are less likely to have children - someone born in 1950 would have been in their 50s by the time same-sex couples could legally adopt - and that they are more likely to be estranged from their families when compared to their heterosexual counterparts.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: The report also found more than half of gay and bisexual men aged 65 and above live alone, compared with less than a quarter of heterosexual men.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Bisexual women aged 50 to 64 are twice as likely as their heterosexual peers to live alone.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: Norman came out as bisexual when he was in his 60s and says he relies on "chosen family" to support him But despite having their support while he's relatively independent, Norman says he worries about the prospect of facing discrimination if he needs more formal care as he ages.

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: When Tim died five months after moving into Tonic, Min says his new-found community rallied around him.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: "You're just here, being yourself." While schemes like Kindred House and Tonic are welcomed by Mindy, Norman and Min, the Spotlight on Ageing report warns that, because the older LGBTQ+ population is growing, the demand for specialist services is expected to outstrip supply.

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: There was a 4% rise in the number of heterosexual people aged 50 and above in the same period.
sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.article_title: 'People forget we exist': Why older LGBTQ+ people fear losing identity

sentences.text: For Mindy, who is part of a steering group advising on the plans, knowing there may be more options available in the future is reassuring.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.

sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), says having someone come into the classroom can really "enlighten [children's] motivation... and give them that sense of passion for all the opportunities beyond the classroom".

sentences.text: Although he acknowledges that finding opportunities in rural areas could be more challenging.

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.article_title: Teenagers to be offered new vocational GCSE subjects in school

sentences.text: Erin Bleakley led a wave of protest after having her exam results downgraded A student whose exam results were downgraded during Covid says she still wants answers from education bosses after their decisions changed the trajectory of her life.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin Bleakley's plans were ruined after she was awarded Bs, Cs and Ds in her highers in 2020 after an emergency marking system was introduced.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Despite her results being eventually adjusted, she never got the A grades her prelims suggested she would get and she had to change course.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: As former SQA head Fiona Robertson prepares to give evidence to the Scottish Covid Inquiry later, Erin wants someone to take accountability for what happened.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin (centre) led protests against the exam results algorithm After lockdown came into force in March 2020 and schools were closed to pupils , teachers were instructed by the Scottish Qualifications Authority (SQA) to estimate exam grades for pupils.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: A later review , external found there was no consistency with how this was carried out around the country.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: In June, the SQA then lowered 125,000 of these grades using an algorithm, saying the grades did not tally with the outcomes of previous cohorts at the same schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Public outrage grew when it became apparent that pupils who had gone to schools in deprived areas formed the bulk of students who had their results downgraded from teacher estimates.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Grades were then restored to teacher estimates for those who had been downgraded.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: But by then it was too late for some pupils who had already lost their chance of a specific university course, because they had entered clearing.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Plus, some students were surprised that the restored teacher estimates didn't match  prelim results.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Schools were closed in March 2020 and learning was rushed online Erin, who is from Glasgow, can't forget the moment she opened her exam results in August 2020.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She'd been studying for six Highers and after getting A grades at prelim, was hoping to study veterinary medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I remember being quite excited," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I didn't think anything was going to go wrong.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I thought I'd set myself up really well." Then the postman arrived and Erin remembers opening the envelope, receiving three Bs, one C and two Ds.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "My legs buckled beneath me, I remember feeling I just couldn't believe this had happened," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It did not reflect anything that I'd done over the last two years." Erin had never failed a class in her life.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She said: "I was crying uncontrollably.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I remember my mum just didn't know what to do and my dad came home from work early.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: It was a horrible experience." The story was repeated on social media and among her school friends.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Then she opened Twitter and saw a post from a private-school pupil from an affluent area who was delighted that despite failing all their prelims, they'd just got five A grades.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I remember thinking, something's not right here," Erin said.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "All of my friends and people I know that wanted to do medicine weren't getting the grades that they got in their prelims." Erin organised a Facebook page and set up a protest in Glasgow's George Square.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It felt like my full life had disappeared in front of me.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: And when I started reading into it, I realised it wasn't anything to do with me.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin's adjusted grades were not enough.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: She pivoted to studying human geography.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: Erin says she still wants answers.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It was a massive injustice that people faced.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: I think I would like to know if anybody in any of these deprived areas was consulted before these decisions were made.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "I think there needs to be some sort of accountability in the system.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: "It has still left an impact on people to this day.
sentences.article_title: 'My legs buckled when I opened my exam results during Covid'

sentences.text: So I do think it's important, even just for acknowledgement, to take accountability of what happened and what went wrong." Covid and lockdown caused massive disruption to education in Scottish schools The experience set her off on a different path.

sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The top official at the Department for the Economy (DfE), Ian Snowden, said the universities were facing a reduction of 6% on the opening funding they received in 2024/25.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The potential cuts come as the Northern Ireland Executive remains seven months into the financial year without a budget.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Snowden said both Queen's University Belfast (QUB) and Ulster University (UU) are expected to have financial deficits in 2025/26.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: With no agreed budget for 2025/26, Stormont departments have been operating under contingency arrangements allowing them to spend up to 95% of last year's funding.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The DfE is the Stormont department with responsibility for higher and further education in Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Universities are mainly funded through student fees and a "teaching grant" provided by DfE.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Further education colleges have already announced big cuts to student places and courses.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Ulster University, meanwhile, is making 450 staff redundant across its campuses to save about £25m.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: The chair of Stormont's economy committee, Democratic Unionist Party assembly member Phillip Brett, said a further cut in university funding could mean that the universities would not receive money for three months for students they have already enrolled.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "The universities have taken students on in the anticipation that they will receive funding from the department," he said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "We're now six months into the financial year and they still haven't received a formal letter of offer from the department.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "And despite students enrolling in September, one of the contingencies from the department is now that come January, February, March you might say 'actually we're not going to pay you for these three months of the students that you've taken on'?" "It's a possibility," Snowden told the committee.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: He also said the universities could only get confirmation of how much funding they would get when the executive agreed a budget.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "At this point we still don't know how much money we have to spend," he said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Amy Smith is the president of the National Union of Students-Union of Students in Ireland Amy Smith, the National Union of Students-Union of Students in Ireland (NUS-USI) president, said it was "disappointing to hear that our universities will be facing cuts to their teaching grants".
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Any cuts directly impact students, their access to their education and the quality of the experience they receive while at university costs to them remain the same," she added.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Students and staff must not be left to shoulder the cost of underfunding.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "We continue to work constructively with the Department for the Economy and government partners to secure a long-term solution that will benefit students and the wider economy," they said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: "Given the deteriorating funding situation from the department, which we regard as very serious, we will continue to enact appropriate caution in relation to our finances," the spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: They also said 735 university staff had applied for voluntary redundancy.
sentences.article_title: Universities face 'substantial' funding cuts amid budget delay

sentences.text: Many pupils at Mitchell House Special School in east Belfast are non-verbal but that does not mean they cannot communicate.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: And to get that message across they have written and recorded a song called My Voice.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: It aims to educate people about alternative communication like Makaton, eye gaze and electronic devices and those who use them.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: The lyrics and music to My Voice were written by the "Moon" Class in Mitchell House School, made up of pupils from 11 to 13 years-old.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "Sometimes my voice is confident, sometimes my voice is calm, sometimes I use my talker, to tell you who I am," one of the verses goes.

sentences.text: Katie-Louise said the class are celebrating how they all communicate differently Gemma,12,  was one of those behind the song and she said that she wanted people to be more aware that not everyone communicates the same way.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "The meaning of the song is that we wanted to tell you that no matter how you use your voice, it's still important and that's really the school motto that we wanted to embody," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "And it's really important to me personally being friends with a lot of people who are non-verbal that people understand that they're not actually non-verbal.

sentences.text: "We're celebrating how we all communicate differently," she told BBC News NI.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

Matthew operates an electronic communication device with his eyes The school's deputy head pupil Matthew uses eye gaze to communicate with his friend, the head pupil Caelainn.

sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice
