sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: Principal Miriam Donnan said that they were proud to share the different ways their pupils communicated.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "We want to tell the world that communication is not just about speech," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "We work really closely with our speech and language therapy department here in school to really promote lots of different ways of communicating and we wanted to celebrate that and share that with everybody.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.text: "So the class themselves came up with the idea for the song and the words are all their own that they came up with their teacher Miss Ryan and it's really a lovely celebration of everybody's voice matters." And Gemma wants everyone to know that sometimes a little patience and consideration might be required.
sentences.article_title: Pupils pen special song to give classmates a voice

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: "It just feels like he's being treated like he's not that important because without support, he's not going to make progress, so is he just expected to stay at home all his life?" Callan Lanigan recently turned 18 and now attends a further education college Callan was diagnosed with autism at the age of two.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: He was in a special learning unit in a mainstream school for most of his time at school.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: He currently attends a further education college with support one day a week but his mother accompanies him to local youth clubs a few nights a week.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: "Callan could tell you everything about a computer and how it was built, but he struggles with the social and communication aspects of everyday life," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: There have been a number of campaigns in Northern Ireland in recent years to do more for young people with SEN after they leave school.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: Ema Cubitt is Northern Ireland's Independent Autism Reviewer Northern Ireland's Independent Autism Reviewer says it is "indefensible" that adults with autism were being left to navigate "the most complex of systems" and as a result are often "left in crisis".
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: Ema Cubitt said: "Once that learning disability door is closed and that support is taken away, where do these families go?
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: "Those families who love and support people with the most complex needs are also navigating the most complex systems, and government are well aware of this problem and the issues these families are facing." Sinn Féin MLA Emma Sheerin has previously raised Callan's case in the Northern Ireland Assembly.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: "Callan has just missed that threshold by the tiniest of margins, he has fallen between two stools time and again, leaving him to linger in a wasteland," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum says autistic son, 18, left abandoned and falling through cracks in system

sentences.text: In a statement, the Department of Health said it was aware that young people with autism can present with vulnerabilities similar to those with a learning disability and that further work was needed to meet their needs on a "regional consistent basis".

sentences.text: Stephanie Kerr is one of a number of parents calling for new mandatory measures For Stephanie Kerr's five-year-old son Caolán many foods come with a serious risk.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "Caolán's allergic to milk, egg, wheat, oat, cumin, tuna, strawberry," she said.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "We have a running joke that it would be quicker listing what he's not allergic to so that's just some of them." Kerr is one of a number of parents calling for new mandatory measures in schools to keep pupils like Caolán safe.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: In England, Benedict's law came into force in September, requiring all schools to follow strengthened allergy guidelines including training for staff and storing equipment like life-saving allergy pens.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: It was named after Benedict Blythe, who died aged five after accidental exposure to cow's milk protein while at Barnack Primary School, near Peterborough, in December 2021.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: The Education Minister, Paul Givan, has committed to a consultation on a similar change in Northern Ireland to introduce stronger allergy guidance for Northern Ireland schools.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: At present though, the onus is mainly on parents and individual schools to ensure safety measures for pupils are in place.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: Stephanie Kerr was one of several parents and experts in Regent House School in Newtownards on Friday training teachers about safety for pupils with severe allergies.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: And that meant confronting some fears.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "I find it difficult as well sometimes talking about the reactions that Caolán has had in the past and what could potentially happen in the future," she said.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: Niamh Kennedy's three children have allergies Niamh Kennedy has three children who have food allergies and she is the chair of Food Allergy NI, the voluntary group who organised the training.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "Our eldest is the most severe.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: He's had anaphylaxis in the past," she said.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "We're very reliant here at the moment on goodwill, individual school policies and individual awareness so it's very much left to up to the school to initiate and to design what works for them.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "But the problem with that is that there's huge variation." She estimates that about two children in every class could have a food allergy and said that, aside from school canteens and packed lunches, risks could lurk in expected places.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "One of the things that we experience as a campaigning group is that most people understand that food allergies need to be considered at mealtimes, but it can be the other moments in the day that can sort of be underestimated," she said.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "Things like making cakes or buns or using crafts.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "This is a potentially life-threatening medical condition." Tracey Dunn said some of the most common foods that can trigger anaphylaxis are milk, fish and eggs That point was reinforced by Tracey Dunn, from the Allergy UK incorporating Anaphylaxis UK organisation, who also spoke to teachers at Regent House School.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "Anaphylaxis is the most serious form of an allergic reaction that can be fatal," she said.
sentences.article_title: Parents call for tougher measures in schools to tackle allergies

sentences.text: "During anaphylaxis the airways are closing and blood pressure is dropping and that leads a person to have symptoms where they are unable to breathe or have noisy breathing or they develop a persistent cough where their voice changes.

While most people may be aware of nut allergies or the risk of shock from insect stings, other common foods can also pose a risk to some people.

sentences.text: US Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald vowed to pursue all those involved In May 2024, Francis Mogambi arrived in the United States after winning the Diversity Visa lottery, a programme that gives people from around the world a chance to become permanent residents.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Just over two years later, the Kenyan national found himself at the centre of a US investigation into an alleged nationwide scheme to defraud the federal student aid system.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: On 19 October 2026, a grand jury in Nebraska indicted Mogambi on five counts of theft of government money and five counts of aggravated identity theft.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors allege that, between November 2025 and May 2026, he worked with associates in Kenya to steal the identities of US citizens and use them to fraudulently enroll fictitious students in American colleges.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Once the fake students were enrolled, Mogambi allegedly diverted their financial aid payments to himself, keeping 30% and sending the remainder to his associates in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The intended loss in his case was $20,000 (£15,000), according to prosecutors.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Court documents say Mogambi received $2,000 a week and attempted to recruit another person into the scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He allegedly told the individual he needed a business that would allow him to cash larger cheques without paying taxes.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Mogambi was arrested shortly after the indictment was returned and is being held in custody pending trial.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He has not yet commented on the allegations against him.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: His case forms part of a wider US investigation, dubbed Operation Ghostbusters, into the alleged use of stolen identities to enrol fictitious students at colleges and claim federal financial aid that resulted in a loss of $130m in taxpayers funds.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: US authorities say the investigation has so far resulted in five indictments that involved Kenyan nationals, while a further 40 investigations remain open.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Hundreds of people have been affected after fraudsters allegedly stole their personally identifiable information (PII) and used it to access federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The stolen personal information was sometimes sold online for between $4 and $8, with fraudsters targeting low-income Americans who had never had the opportunity to attend college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At a news conference on 29 October announcing the first charges in the investigation, Assistant Attorney General Colin M McDonald, who heads the Justice Department's National Fraud Enforcement Division, vowed to pursue those involved.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "If you steal taxpayers' dollars, if you exploit a programme meant to help students, we are resolved to find you and prosecute you," he said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department says those behind the fraud use what is described as "super intelligence" to place fake students in classrooms and complete coursework, creating the impression that they are attending college and allowing financial aid payments to continue.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "The goal is to keep the ghost student in school as long as possible.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Semester after semester after semester stealing money from the taxpayers," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: But the consequences extend beyond the financial losses suffered by the US government.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: People whose identities are stolen can find themselves facing unexpected student loan debts, even if they have never enrolled in college.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "His identity was stolen, his credit is now at risk, and his name is on the bill," McDonald said, describing the impact on one victim.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: He also said that nearly a third of community college applicants in California in 2024 had been identified as fraudulent.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The scale of the suspected fraud is significant.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Investigators identified 830,840 potentially fraudulent Federal Student Aid identification numbers associated with nearly $130m in September and October 2026.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: They recommended that the Department of Education disable them.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The figure represents financial aid associated with potentially fraudulent accounts, not confirmed losses.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: "In a flash, the money vanishes, often overseas in places like Kenya," McDonald said.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The investigation has also exposed alleged financial links between the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In September, US officials travelled to Kenya to work with local law enforcement on extraditions, prosecutions and the recovery of money allegedly stolen from American taxpayers.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: With the help of Kenyan investigators, US authorities seized more than $750,000  from a cryptocurrency account belonging to a Kenyan national connected to the wider scheme.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The Justice Department described it as the first international seizure of its kind in Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: The seizure was not connected to Mogambi's individual case.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: In a separate case in Virginia, prosecutors allege that a Kenyan national received more than 700 fraudulent student-aid refunds totalling approximately $1.44m.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: At least $1.3m was subsequently transferred through thousands of transactions to accounts in the US and Kenya.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Meanwhile, in New Jersey, three people have been charged with allegedly acting as money mules in a scheme to obtain more than $1m in federal student aid.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Prosecutors say they received the funds through US bank accounts, kept a portion for themselves and transferred the remainder to alleged co-conspirators in Kenya linked to a purported safari company.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: If convicted, Mogambi faces a mandatory prison term of at least 10 years, according to the Justice Department.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Authorities say those convicted will also face appropriate orders for forfeiture of assets and restitution to victims, in addition to any prison sentences.
sentences.article_title: How Kenyans got caught in $130m US ghost student scam

sentences.text: Eddie Lever was able to leave his tenancy more easily because of the Renters' Rights Act When the Renters' Rights Act came into force in May it was described as the biggest change for tenants in England in a generation, giving more stability and security to the millions of people who rent from private landlords.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation has also prompted a shake-up of the student rental market, which has posed challenges for landlords as it allows people to leave a tenancy rather than being tied in for the full academic year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: Eddie Lever had finished his first year at the University of Exeter when he decided the course wasn't for him.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The 20-year-old wanted to switch to studying international relations at the University of York but had already organised his house for the upcoming year.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The tenancy was signed and had started.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: But because of changes in the Renters' Rights Act, Eddie only had to give two months' notice before he could leave and stop paying rent.
sentences.article_title: Students like new tenancy freedoms - but landlords warn of higher rents

sentences.text: The legislation ended fixed-term tenancies - where renters are tied in to contracts for a specific number of months.

sentences.text: One user said Apple had helped him to replace his faulty iPhone Duo Apple has acknowledged some of its iPhone Duo handsets have developed problems with their screens, just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: Photos posted on social media show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant's first ever foldable device , which has a starting price of £1,999 ($2,668) in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: Apple said it was aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: The Duo's launch, which attracted crowds at Apple stores around the world last week, is an attempt to reinvigorate the brand's device range and challenge the foldable phones made by rivals.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: The extent of the issue remains unclear.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: Apple did not say how many devices were affected, while some images showing faulty devices may have been created using AI.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: Francisco Jeronimo, technology analyst at market research firm IDC, said that meant some caution was needed before drawing conclusions about the whole production run.
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: But he added the early reports of issues also showed "that even a company with Apple's engineering resources and supply chain discipline faces a steep learning curve in foldables".
sentences.article_title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos affected by screen problem

sentences.text: The Duo's 7.6-inch (19.3cm) inner display is held together by a central hinge - a complex piece of engineering that has resulted in similar flaws in folding devices made by some of Apple's competitors.

sentences.text: Samsung's first foldable phone, the Galaxy Fold, suffered an early setback in 2019 when reviewers reported broken screens on the devices.

sentences.text: "Apple has a loyal customer base and a retail network that can swap devices on the spot, but with a further 28 markets launching on 30 October, it needs to clarify its warranty position quickly," he said.

sentences.text: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has become a key figure in the current AI era.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic just released the required paperwork ahead of its long-anticipated debut on the US stock market.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The 335-page document included fresh details of how the Claude chatbot owner makes money, what it spends that money on and who it is controlled by.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic also detailed some of the risks it claimed AI technology poses, including how it could take human lives.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: That information sat alongside the many purported benefits of the technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Here are five key points worth highlighting from the filing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Every public company has to tell potential investors how things could go wrong.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's "risk factors" were unique, also disclosing how the AI technology it is developing could doom humanity as a whole.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity," Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: It noted that less than a year ago, a hacking group Anthropic believed to be sponsored by China "manipulated" Claude to successfully intrude on a number of institutions, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies and government agencies.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But Anthropic said its success is dependent on its ability to constantly "develop, improve, and deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: One of the most significant risks to that ability is Anthropic's access to infrastructure it needs, including computer chips and data centres, to build, train and operate the models that underpin its technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic has yet to disclose a target share price for its stock listing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company is widely expected to debut with a market valuation of $2 trillion or more, making it the largest stock listing in history.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But the figure will be heavily influenced by its financial performance.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic lost $80.7bn (£60bn) in the first half of this year, double what it lost across 2025 altogether.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company's overall revenue was $16.2bn for the six-month period.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Revenues are rising rapidly, but the firm has a long way to go before it breaks even.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Troy Hooper, co-head of equity capital markets at Mergermarket, said Anthropic's revenue growth is "exceptional".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: But investors are "less forgiving" of tech companies promising huge future returns than they were even months ago, he added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's debt picture is also unclear given it has a huge amount of accounting charges related to certain forms of investment.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "As a result, investors do not yet have a clear view of Anthropic's underlying profitability or whether its rate of cash generation is sufficient to support the business as it scales," Hooper added.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Despite losing money, Anthropic has heaps of cash lying about.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: At $131.6bn, almost all of its cash in hand is defined as "working capital", meaning it can use the money to fund its operations day-to-day.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Currently, Anthropic has more cash on hand than Meta and Google combined.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic's costs could rise as it faces fierce competition for top staff and computing power from other AI giants.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The leasing of data centres alone is set to cost the company $321.4bn through agreements struck so far this year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Hooper said such large costs are expected to grow.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Even with this kind of cash, it won't be enough to maintain its business growth.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Any investors in Anthropic "will be paying for future dominance, not present-day economics", he said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic sees boundless ways it can sell its technology to customers.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: A large portion of its current business comes from just 250 major enterprise customers, which it says have paid it at least $10m in the past year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: An even smaller number, just five enterprise customers, make up a quarter of its current business.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founder ETF, pointed out that "many top Anthropic customers have no long-term contract".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The company's level of business concentration leaves Anthropic dependent on a small fraction of its paying customers to support its growth, with no guarantee it will continue.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic also has enterprise relationships with the likes of Google and Amazon, both of which are also investors in the company "and competitors", creating potential business conflicts in the future, Monaghan noted.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic said its overall enterprise customer base has grown rapidly, going from roughly 1,500 customers last year to almost 12,000 this year.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Part of its growth strategy is offering Claude tools for free before working to "convert these users into paying customers over time".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The strategy has led to Claude seeing "the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history", the company claimed.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: For all of the risks Anthropic has said AI poses, it also reiterated its claim AI will produce an "extraordinary" amount of good.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Achieving our mission means the world gains the enormous benefits of frontier AI while mitigating the most significant risks," the company said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: Anthropic said AI could one day provide individually tailored education and expert financial and legal advice, advance power grids and battery design for greater efficiency and reliability and help the "developing world" build more technological capabilities.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we believe frontier AI will help drive global economic growth," the company said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know

sentences.text: The Confederation of African Football (Caf) will instead retain the tournament's traditional biennial staging, with its president Patrice Motsepe saying the U-turn was based on "advancing, protecting and promoting" the interests of the African game.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: The first indication that the frequency of Afcon was being reconsidered came at Caf's strategy conference in Cape Verde earlier this month.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Questions are now being asked about the decision-making process and what this means for the future of African football.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Afcon has predominantly been held every two years since its first edition in 1957, barring two three-year gaps in the 1960s and one year between the 2012 and 2013 tournaments.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: On the eve of the 2025 finals in Morocco, Motsepe announced all that would change from 2028.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: The South African said the shift to a four-year cycle was, in part, to help the global calendar "be significantly more synchronised and harmonised".
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: In recent years Afcon has been staged midway through the European club season, leading to recurring disputes over the release of African players.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Fifa general secretary Mattias Grafstrom was sitting aside Motsepe when the plan was announced, and critics highlighted that the scheduling change favoured football's world governing body more than the African game.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: "I think the general sentiment around the continent has been that the two-year cycle has served the continent very well," Football Association of Zambia (Faz) official Sydney Mungala told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: In its stead, an annual Africa Nations League involving all 54 countries on the continent was proposed.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Motsepe described the ambition as creating a "world-class competition every year".
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: The idea was to move beyond Caf's heavy reliance on Afcon and develop a more sustainable commercial model which could support football development.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Yet the last time an ambitious alternative competition took place in Africa, it failed to deliver on its financial promise and was quickly ditched.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: The Africa Super League, announced by Caf in 2022 to revolutionise continental club competition, and with projected annual revenues of $200m (£149m), was discontinued after just one edition.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Motsepe later acknowledged that commercial deals fell short of expectations.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: "We didn't proceed as quickly because the partners that were giving us money were not giving us the deals we thought we would be happy with," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: The decision to move to a four-year cycle was taken at a meeting of Caf's executive committee last December - without being tabled at a general assembly where all member nations are represented.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: "These kinds of decisions should be put to the general assembly, they should be debated and discussed for months at a time," Algerian journalist Maher Mezahi told the BBC.

sentences.text: "Afcon is the locomotive by which Caf funds all of its other competitions." Caf subsequently asked its 54 associations to express a preference between proceeding with the four-year format or retaining the original schedule, and the executive committee eventually voted to restore the status quo.
sentences.article_title: Why has Caf abandoned plans to hold Afcon every four years?

sentences.text: Motsepe said the decision was in the "best interest of African football" and would contribute to the development and growth of the sport.

sentences.text: A lot has changed for football managers over the past few decades but Vincent Kompany's recent health scare was a reminder it is still an all-consuming occupation that takes its toll physically and mentally.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: From the tragic death of Scotland manager Jock Stein after a World Cup qualifier against Wales in 1985, to the different heart issues suffered by Graeme Souness, Sir Alex Ferguson, Gerard Houllier, Joe Kinnear and Harry Redknapp down the years, I've always been aware of the dangers of my job.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: It is 25 years since then Leicester boss Dave Bassett and Bolton manager Sam Allardyce took part in an experiment that saw them wired up to heart monitors during a game between the teams, and both their heart rates reached critical levels.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: It's not just during games when management can have an adverse effect on your health, either.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: The stress you are under is relentless and you have to find a way of looking after yourself.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Fortunately this was something I realised very early on in my management career.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: In those days, and in fact throughout my whole career, I wanted to be the person who made all the footballing decisions at my club.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: That meant I did everything from scouting players to signing the ones I wanted, and organised my staff at every level from first-team to the reserve and youth teams, all within the club's financial restraints.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I saw the first-team performances as being my main responsibility so I never wavered from my work on the training ground either, coaching a certain way that suited the players and gave them the best chance of winning games - which would ultimately determine my future.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: All of the above was generally the way most English clubs were run so it was not just me doing it.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: But the demands were relentless, and I had to learn how to look after myself properly to cope.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: During those early days, my management of myself personally was really poor.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: It starts with your diet.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: At that time I would be driving up and down the motorway to watch players, trying to find a fish and chip shop or fuelled only by a half-time pie or a sandwich from a local shop.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I was young and could deal with it, so it never crossed my mind that I wasn't eating well or getting the exercise I needed to retain my own fitness levels.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: But, at the same time, the pressure on the team to win games ultimately fell on my shoulders so the pressure of being the person responsible for results and performances every week really built up.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I had never realised how stressful that part of management was until we started to lose a few games and every bit of criticism was directed on to my lap.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: That part has not changed for managers now.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: They may have less to do with the way their clubs are run now but they still have to deal with people they have never met criticising their ability to do a job they love to media outlets, without taking into consideration any other factors that might be contributing to those performances and results.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: That's why it's so stressful.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: All the arrows and guns are pointed in your direction, and you have no way of protecting yourself, apart from by winning games.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Pulis was player-coach at Bournemouth under Harry Redknapp before getting his first management job with the Cherries at the age of 34, when Redknapp left for West Ham in 1992 Many a young manager will have experienced these factors, which could and would affect their health and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: The turning point for me came when I spoke to an Australian triathlete just before I left Bournemouth in 1994.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: His advice was pretty blunt and straightforward.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: He told me doing my job was physically hampering my own fitness levels - but more worrying were the stress levels that came with it, because they could have a major effect on my life itself.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: It was only after having that conversation that I realised the compromises I was making for my career at the cost of my own health.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I came to the conclusion that in my next job, if I got one, I would dedicate myself to a more manageable lifestyle and put my own fitness first.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I decided I would work out early every morning before breakfast at the club I managed, so I could then dedicate the rest of my day to my work.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Yes, there were days I would be empty and would only walk and stretch, but generally I stuck to that rule and worked hard to keep on top of myself physically.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: At Gillingham in 1999, I decided to run a marathon - my first London Marathon - which got me focused during the season in respect of my physical health.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: That was my first challenge of many I have taken on for charity down the years.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I have also cycled from John O' Groats to Land's End, walked up Mount Kilimanjaro, and rowed from Tower Bridge to the Eiffel Tower.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: All of this exercise also helped my stress levels, especially in respect of sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Being tired going to bed really helped my sleeping hours and meant I was never kept awake worrying about what was going wrong at work.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: There were other ways I looked after my mental health too.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Even as the internet exploded, I have never read any press, good or bad, about me or my team.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I always worked as hard I could at every club I was with, and picked good staff who I was able to confide in, but I was able to switch off too, thanks to my family.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: I've written in previous columns about my routine after games and how I would often drive home to the south coast on a Saturday night, reflecting on our result and starting my preparation for our next game.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: But Sundays were always about spending all day with the family.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Whether it was watching my son Anthony playing football as a young boy, or just being around the children full stop, that was how I relaxed and that day with them became a release valve which was an important part of my routine.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: West Brom captain Darren Fletcher presented Pulis with a Ship's Decanter at the club's training ground to commemorate his 1,000th match as a manager, the day before they drew 1-1 with his old club Stoke When I speak to young managers now, I give them the same advice I followed.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: You have to maintain your enthusiasm for looking after yourself, because this is the time when you will need it the most.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Under the constant stress you will put yourself under, it is dangerous not to.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: But, while everyone knows the risks of the job, many are prepared to take them.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Years ago, managers' health was never much of a concern to clubs - we probably drank too much and ate too many of the wrong foods, at all hours of the day and night, but that was just part of the lifestyle that went with it.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Now, there is lots more support - the League Managers' Association offers frequent health testing under its 'Fit To Manage' programme, and most clubs' medical staff will now ensure that not only are their players properly looked after, the coaching staff is too.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: A manager's life can still be a lonely place, but thankfully the help available is on a different level to where it was at the start of my career.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.
sentences.article_title: Why managers must put their own health first - Pulis

sentences.text: Since the end of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia have won the men's World Championship five times but have never claimed the women's title Ukraine's ice hockey federation has expressed "deep outrage" at Russia being allowed to compete in international events again.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) overturned the ban placed on Russia by the sport's global governing body, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and earlier this year the IIHF ruled they would remain excluded.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: The Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) appealed that decision to Cas, which has upheld it following an in-person hearing at its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: In a statement, the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said it "respected the authority and status of Cas".
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: "At the same time, we express our deep outrage at this decision," it added.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: It said the threats, which had formed the basis of the ban, had not disappeared, adding "against this background, the decision to allow Russian teams to international hockey competitions causes special outrage".
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: A statement from Cas , external said that arguments made by the IIHF "citing safety, security and other concerns" were "not supported by sufficient evidence".
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: Russia are now set to be part of IIHF events in the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: Ukraine's men have qualified for the top flight world championships for the first time in 20 years after winning promotion at this year's Division 1 tournament in Poland.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: The IIHF would not confirm whose place Russia could potentially take but pointed to its statement which said: "The ruling also has significant practical implications for competitions already at an advanced stage of preparation.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: "These decisions made by Cas do not consider the practical elements which cannot be implemented immediately." Individual athletes from Russia were allowed to compete at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Italy under a neutral flag, although not in ice hockey.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: The IIHF expressed "disappointment" , external with the ruling.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: "The IIHF disagrees with this aspect of the ruling and maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions," they said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: "Allowing Russia to participate entails significant security-related, political, and economic consequences for us as hosts.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: We are now evaluating the ruling together with the IIHF and will provide information regarding the next steps." The United Kingdom, Finnish and Czech federations also condemned the decision to allow Russia to enter teams.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: Jan Cerny, secretary general of Czech Ice Hockey said he "very unpleasantly surprised" by the decision adding: "The current stance of Czech ice hockey does not change with the CAS decision.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's 'deep outrage' after Russia's international ice hockey ban ended

sentences.text: We do not agree with Russia's participation in IIHF tournaments during the war of aggression in Ukraine." The chairman of the Finnish Ice Hockey Federation, Heikki Hietanen, called the ruling "in it's entirety, incomprehensible".

sentences.text: Yiech Pur Biel (left) is leading the first ever refugee team at the Youth Olympics When he started running, Yiech Pur Biel had to compete barefoot.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Far from home in a new country, it was the first step towards rebuilding his life as a refugee.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: "That's when I decided now it is time to depend on myself and also to start a new life with determination," he tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: In 2016, Biel made history competing in the 800m event as part of the first Olympic refugee team at the Rio summer Olympics in Brazil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Ten years on, he's making history again leading the first refugee team for the Youth Olympics as their Chef de Mission.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Joining almost 3,000 athletes, the small team of six will be wanting to make sure their debut counts - but Biel says they're also hoping to send a message that "refugees still need our help".
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Hosted in Senegal, Saturday's opening ceremony will launch the first ever Olympic sporting event on African soil.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Africa is home to nearly 45 million displaced people, out of almost 120 million globally, representing the world's biggest displacement crisis.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Biel says for the refugee team, the Youth Olympics is "a chance for them to tell the world and also to represent the population, especially the refugee population, in Africa".
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: He ended up in Kenya, telling BBC Newsbeat: "It traumatised me, starting a new life, being alone in Kakuma," referring to the major refugee settlement close to the border between Kenya and South Sudan.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: "But I started a new life, I believe that school helped me a lot.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: It helped me to interact with young people who faced the same challenges." The rest of his childhood was spent on the refugee camp where he took an interest in football.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: After realising it wasn't the sport for him, he gave running a go during trials set up by the International Olympic Committee - where he raced without shoes.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: It made him "believe that if I can work harder by myself, I can achieve", he says.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Arno Yafunga Botay is one of six athletes competing for the Refugee Olympic Team at the Dakar 2026 Youth Games One of the athletes on the refugee team, Arno Yafunga Botay, also lived at Kakuma after fleeing his home in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2017, when he was six.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: Now 15, he will be competing in judo and told BBC Sport Africa he's promised to bring back a gold medal which he'd like to take to the refugee camp.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: "I think if I achieve [a] gold medal, I can go there and teach them the value of judo," he said.
sentences.article_title: Refugee athlete to make history for second time at Youth Olympics

sentences.text: As for Biel, he says it's an honour to be chosen as the team's Chef de Mission.

sentences.text: More than 800,000 were killed in the 1994 Rwandan genocide A Rwandan man has been convicted in the US of lying under oath about his involvement in the 1994 genocide during the trial of a former university classmate.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: A federal jury in Boston found Eric Nshimiye, 54, guilty of perjury and obstruction of justice charges stemming from his testimony in the 2019 immigration fraud trial of Jean Leonard Teganya, who was also accused of participating in the atrocities.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: Nshimiye fled Rwanda for Kenya in 1994 and was admitted to the US as a refugee the following year.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: About 800,000 people, mostly from Rwanda's minority Tutsi community, were killed by ethnic Hutu extremists during the 100-day genocide.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: Rwanda's 100 days of slaughter Prosecutors said Nshimiye concealed his involvement in the genocide to secure entry into the country.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: Evidence presented at his trial showed that, while a student at the University of Rwanda in Butare, he took part in attacks of the Tutsi people, including by striking them on the head with a club.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: He faces up to five years in prison for each of the four perjury counts and a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for obstruction of justice.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: He is due to be sentenced on 26 January 2027.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: "For nearly three decades, this defendant concealed his involvement in the 1994 Rwandan genocide and the heinous acts of violence he committed, including clubbing people to death," US justice department prosecutor Tysen Duva said.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: "Then he lied to immigration officials in order to become a US citizen, and he lied to a federal jury to protect himself and a fellow perpetrator of the Rwandan genocide," Duva said.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: Nshimiye's lawyer, Kurt Kerns, said in a statement that they were "obviously ⁠disappointed with the verdict" and would pursue "all avenues of relief".

sentences.text: He also said Nshimaye was charged only after testifying as a character witness for Teganya, his former university classmate.
sentences.article_title: US convicts Rwandan man who hid genocide role for decades

sentences.text: A sunscreen safety scandal sparked massive backlash in Australia, which has the highest rate of skin cancer in the world Australian sunscreen manufacturers will be subject to stricter rules in the wake of a safety scandal that saw popular brands pulled off shelves.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: The reforms, announced by the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) on Tuesday, include stronger testing and quality requirements for specific ingredients.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: This comes after a bombshell report last year by consumer advocacy group Choice which found that some popular sunscreens did not provide the level of protection their manufacturers claimed.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: The new proposed regulations are "about making SPF claims more reliable" and giving the agency "faster access to evidence when concerns arise", Robyn Langham, the TGA's chief medical adviser, tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: "Australians expect the SPF on the label to be backed by robust evidence," she said in a statement over email.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: This is to ensure "clear distinction for consumers" between sunscreens that are mainly made for UV protection and cosmetic products where UV protection is a secondary function.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: Suppliers would also be required to provide their SPF testing data to the TGA when they list a sunscreen, and keep periodically testing the product throughout its shelf life.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: Under current regulations, it's not mandatory for sunscreen manufacturers to provide testing data to the TGA unless requested.
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal

sentences.text: The TGA said the reforms would be "implemented in stages, with further consultation where required".
sentences.article_title: Australian sunscreen brands face stricter rules after safety scandal
